content.comment_body: Hello everyone, This is my first attempt at building a circuit with a PLC, and I'm curious if any issues might arise if I switch off the system daily simply by disconnecting the power while a program is still running. Is this safe for the system, or do I need to follow any special shutdown process before cutting the power? When I turn the system back on the next day, will the program automatically start from the beginning? Kind regards! Ps. My system is a: [company_name] [product_name] [article_no]
Yes, the system restarts each time you switch on the supply voltage. For some blocks, you can enable retentivity so they preserve their state or values after restarting.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is asking about the correct way to power off a [company_name] [product_name] PLC and whether removing power while running poses problems. Other users confirm it is safe to simply disconnect power, as the device restarts automatically upon power-up. However, unless configured with retentive settings, the system does not preserve block states across shutdowns, which may affect behavior after reboot.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a simple, reliable way to turn off the PLC and reassurance that the program will function correctly when powered on again. They also want to know if any program data or states will be lost after shutdown.
